content.text:
Changing the props of `TelegramLinkWidget` affects two pages. Both render it directly, and both currently pass only `role`.

| Page | Route | Usage |
|---|---|---|
| `app/portal/reseller/page.tsx:741` | `/portal/reseller` | `<TelegramLinkWidget role="reseller" />` |
| `app/portal/supplier/page.tsx:715` | `/portal/supplier` | `<TelegramLinkWidget role="supplier" />` |

The component is defined in `app/portal/components/TelegramLinkWidget.tsx`, with its props in `TelegramLinkWidgetProps` at line 17. No other pages import it.

**Tests:** `test/portal-telegram-widget.test.ts` creates the component with `{ role: "reseller" }` and `{ role: "supplier" }`. It also has two tests that check the reseller and supplier overview pages embed the widget. Update these if you rename or remove `role`, or add a required prop.

**Layouts:** Both pages sit under their own `layout.tsx` files, but those don't use the widget, so they are unaffected.

If you add an optional prop, nothing breaks. If you rename or remove `role`, or add a required prop, you must update both call sites. TypeScript will flag any call site you miss.

I didn't open the component file, so I haven't checked how `role` is used inside it. I also haven't checked the widget's internal API calls, which go to `/api/v2/auth/telegram/*`.
